titleStmt.title: Exhaustive studies before covid-19 pandemic attack of students’ conceptual change in science education: A literature review
titleStmt.author: Ananda Hafizhah Putri
Achmad Samsudin
Andi Suhandi

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Exhaustive studies before covid-19 pandemic attack of students’ conceptual change in science education: A literature review

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: critique
span.quote: Based on findings, the most noticeable trend in the current literature is that instructional studies in science education used theoretical and methodological frameworks that are now considered outdated.

span.label: students' conceptual change in science education
span.quote: Educational researchers develop instructional approaches that support students’ efforts to restructure their prior knowledge, a process called conceptual change.

span.label: systematic-review
span.quote: This systematic review is aimed to explore the researches that established students’ conceptual change process, both studies that facilitate conceptual change and studies that determined learner characters influencing conceptual change.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: COVID-19 disrupted teaching and research activity and diverted attention to building online/hybrid learning environments, which is why no conceptual change study appears in the 2020-2021 window
span.quote: As an effect of COVID-19 pandemic, academics and researchers have faced unpredicted and continuous disruptions in their teaching and research activities.

span.label: Studies that found a conception and no change were excluded, so the corpus is selected on the outcome the review reports.
span.quote: researches that merely identified students' alternative beliefs, not whether or not they were changed by a specific intervention

span.label: The review's own verdict is that one framework across the literature determined how the construct was measured.
span.quote: The most significant theoretical limitation was that nearly all of the studies observed conceptual change from a cognitive-only framework which led into examining of conceptual change itself quantitatively

span.label: The corpus is what a keyword search returned, narrowed by hand from hundreds to fifty.
span.quote: Hundreds of documents were discovered. Yet, only 50 articles matched our criteria

span.label: The selection required an intervention aimed at conceptions, which fixes the kind of study that can appear.
span.quote: Our two primary criteria in selecting article to review are studies in the field of science education and to use the certain treatments to measure or improve student’s conceptions

span.label: conceptual change
span.quote: Conceptual change as a cognitive variable was measured or described in many methods

span.label: misconception
span.quote: Misconceptions develop when pupils assign concepts to wrong ontological categories

span.label: alternative conception
span.quote: the students enter the classrooms with pre-instructional alternative conceptions

span.label: learning gains
span.quote: The most used were using profile of conception/understanding, remediation of misconception and learning gains

span.label: ontological categories
span.quote: pupils assign concepts to wrong ontological categories

span.label: conceptual change - AS A COGNITIVE VARIABLE WITH A MEASUREMENT MENU: what the reviewed studies actually recorded was a profile of conception or understanding, remediation of misconception, or learning gains, nearly always from a pre- and post-test
span.quote: Conceptual change as a cognitive variable was measured or described in many methods. The most used were using profile of conception/understanding, remediation of misconception and learning gains

span.label: misconception - AS A CATEGORY ERROR: on the classical model a misconception is a concept assigned to the wrong ontological category, so change means altering what kind of thing the student takes the concept to be - a definition that makes some disagreements invisible
span.quote: Misconceptions develop when pupils assign concepts to wrong ontological categories, according to one distinction in the classical conceptual change model (Chi, Slotta, & De Leeuw, 1994). Conceptual change, according to this viewpoint, occurs when students alter their perceptions

span.label: the same object under several names - students arrive with prior ideas called alternative conceptions here, alternative beliefs in the exclusion rule, and misconceptions in the classical model, with no statement anywhere that the three are the same thing
span.quote: Science education researchers have obviously documented that the students enter the classrooms with pre-instructional alternative conceptions (Broughton, Sinatra, & Reynolds, 2010; Diakidoy et al., 2016; Vosniadou & Skopeliti, 2005;). These prior conceptions are often incomplete or incorrect

span.label: builds-on → Randolph (2009) literature-review procedure, as used by Mills, Thomas & Lewthwaite (2016)
span.quote: Researchers adapted procedures from Randolph (2009) for reviewing the literature in this investigation as Mills, Thomas, & Lewthwaite (2016) did in their review.

span.label: conceptual change —operationalised-as→ learning gains
span.quote: Conceptual change as a cognitive variable was measured or described in many methods. The most used were using profile of conception/understanding, remediation of misconception and learning gains

span.label: misconception —operationalised-as→ ontological categories
span.quote: Misconceptions develop when pupils assign concepts to wrong ontological categories, according to one distinction in the classical conceptual change model

span.label: Across the 50 reviewed studies, physics was the science domain most often targeted by conceptual change research, ahead of the other science domains.
span.quote: Physics disciplines have received more attention than other science domains

span.label: Newtonian mechanics was the single most frequently examined physics topic in the reviewed conceptual change studies.
span.quote: The most widely examined physics concept was Newtonian Mechanics.

span.label: Undergraduate students from a range of majors, not only science education students, were the most common participants in the reviewed studies.
span.quote: Most studies were conducted on undergraduate students with various majors, not only science education programme.

span.label: Quasi-experimental designs comparing treatments between groups dominated the reviewed conceptual change research.
span.quote: The majority of studies used a quasi-experimental study design

span.label: Method was dominated by pre- and post-testing of small groups with quantitatively analysed data.
span.quote: Another obvious trend is that research method used in these studies was dominated with pre- and post-test with small group and data collection was obtained and analysed quantitatively.

span.label: Nearly all reviewed studies framed conceptual change from a cognitive-only perspective, which in turn pushed them to measure conceptual change quantitatively - the review's main theoretical criticism of the field.
span.quote: The most significant theoretical limitation was that nearly all of the studies observed conceptual change from a cognitive-only framework which led into examining of conceptual change itself quantitatively.

span.label: Although the search window ran to 2021, the review found no conceptual change study published during the 2020-2021 pandemic period.
span.quote: Consequently, conceptual change study was not found in period 2020-2021.

span.label: Only five of the fifty reviewed studies examined the conceptual change of pre-service teachers or in-service teachers, leaving that population largely unstudied.
span.quote: From the review, only five studies that examined both pre-service teacher’s and teacher’s conceptual changes.

span.label: Affective, metacognitive and other non-cognitive variables were assessed almost entirely through refutation texts, questionnaires or interviews rather than through instructional interventions designed around them.
span.quote: In terms of affective, metacognitive and other domains, they were examined through refutation texts, related questionnaire or interviews.

span.label: conceptual change
span.quote: Educational researchers develop instructional approaches that support students’ efforts to restructure their prior knowledge, a process called conceptual change.

span.label: conceptual change instructional intervention (texts, cognitive conflict, simulations, learning models)
span.term: conceptual change instructional intervention (texts, cognitive conflict, simulations, learning models)
span.quote: The reviewed researches conducted several instructional interventions for conceptual change to improve students’ misconceptions of science materials

span.label: students' conceptual change
span.quote: data of conceptual change was nearly generated by pre- and post-test.

span.label: affective and motivational variables (emotion, interest, self-efficacy, attitude)
span.term: affective and motivational variables (emotion, interest, self-efficacy, attitude)
span.quote: It is hypothesized that several emotional and motivational variables play an important part in learning about conceptual changes.

span.label: 50 studies — number of articles that met the inclusion criteria and were synthesised in the review
span.quote: Overall, 50 studies were examined in this review.

span.label: only 50 articles — how many of the hundreds of retrieved documents survived screening
span.quote: Hundreds of documents were discovered. Yet, only 50 articles matched our criteria as will be

span.label: 2011 to 2021 — publication window covered by the reviewed studies
span.quote: The researches chosen for review spanned from 2011 to 2021 (as shown in Figure 1).

span.label: 7 weeks — duration of the review/synthesis activity itself (22 September to 3 November 2021)
span.quote: The review activity of this study conducted for 7 weeks from September 22nd to November 3rd,

span.label: three studies — number of reviewed studies using a purely qualitative (case study/interview) approach
span.quote: Then, only three studies used qualitative approach in form of case study

span.label: five studies — number of reviewed studies that examined pre-service teachers' and teachers' conceptual change
span.quote: From the review, only five studies that examined both pre-service teacher’s and teacher’s conceptual changes.

span.label: 2018 — peak year for conceptual change publications within the reviewed decade, after which output declined
span.quote: The most number of publications emerged in 2018 and decreased gradually forwards.
